deck_title: Archimedes Hat-Box cylindrical equal-area sampling vs naive equirectangular polar pinching rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Archimedes of Syracuse (c. 225 BCE, On the Sphere and Cylinder) Hat-Box cylindrical equal-area theorem (sampling axial height z = cos(theta) = 1 - 2*xi_1 in [-1, 1] and azimuth phi = 2*pi*xi_2 so parallel-circle shrinkage sin(theta) cancels slant-height stretching 1/sin(theta), locking solid-angle sample density ratio at D = 1.0000x across all 17 latitude-compression stations u in [0.0000, 1.0000] with 0/17 pinched stations) versus naive equirectangular latitude-longitude sampling (theta = pi*xi_1, which shrinks solid-angle elements as dOmega = sin(theta)*dtheta*dphi and crowds sample density per steradian by 1/sin(theta) = 1 + u to 1.2500x at u=0.25, 1.5000x at u=0.50, and 2.0000x at u=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-subband spherical zone surface-area quadrature.
